{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "A's demand evidence points to an underserved sub-segment. The forum quotes describe severe, specific PFIC pain (five-figure remediation costs, people considering renunciation). Every incumbent charges extra for the investor/PFIC case, for example H&R Block's $99 per Form 8621 and Expatfile's $199 Investor tier, and ETO explicitly excludes investors. That gives a focused wedge. B's own brief says none of its sourced complaints are about a missing notes-plus-reminders product, only about price and group-practice friction.",
    "A shows sourced willingness to pay at scale for DIY software: $119–$199 per year, with 165k+ and 100k users claimed on incumbent sites. B's payers are also proven, but B's wedge requires undercutting incumbents already priced from $49/mo (a lower $29 tier is claimed only by third-party sources). It also competes with reminder tools from about $8/mo, which leaves little pricing room.",
    "A has a cheaper, sourced acquisition benchmark: about $40 CAC implied by Expatfile's referral payout. B's only priced channel is a $500/mo Capterra minimum. Organic Reddit outreach in B is unproven and limited by self-promotion norms.",
    "B's compliance burden is heavier and ongoing. It requires HIPAA Business Associate obligations, BAAs with every customer, and a sourced $8k–$25k first-year compliance estimate. A's main regulatory hurdle is IRS e-file authorization, which can take up to 45 days. A could sidestep that at first by launching the narrower PFIC-calculation tool raised in its open questions, which gives A a faster path to a first paying customer within 90 days."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's case rests on a 'price-sensitive solo therapists unhappy with incumbents' segment, drawn from Reddit and competitor-blog complaints. B's brief concedes these complaints are about price and group-practice scaling, not demand for a stripped-down notes-plus-reminders app. It also notes that switching interest is flowing toward other full EHRs. There is no evidence that anyone would pay for B's specific product.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate. Both briefs argue substantially against their own ideas. A has unresolved risks: e-file authorization of up to 45 days, a trust deficit in a high-stakes domain, an unquantified niche size, and demand evidence of only three forum posts, one of which concerns attorney costs rather than software. A wins mainly because B's demand evidence does not support its specific product and B's compliance costs are larger and recurring, not because A is strongly validated."
}
